title: IIDP
bodyHtml:
Integrated Islet Distribution Project (IIDP)

https://iidp.coh.org/

The Integrated Islet Distribution Project (IIDP) promotes basic and translational pancreatic research by distributing samples and data derived from human islets and associated tissues.

Data Types

Biosamples

Cultured viable human islets from donors with type 2 diabetes or no diabetes, flash frozen islets, formalin-fixed native pancreas histology slides, frozen pancreas pieces, pancreatic ductal tissues, peripancreatic lymph nodes, fresh and frozen acinar tissues, duodenal tissues, spleen pieces, plasma, and serum

Donor Information

Donor data from the IIDP Islet Isolation Centers (IIC) and the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS)

Workflows and Standards

Islet isolation metrics from the IIDP IICs

Genotyping

Genetic ancestry and partitioned genetic risk scores for type 1 and type 2 diabetes from the IIDP Human Islet Genotyping Initiative (HIGI)

Cellular Phenotyping

Post-shipment islet phenotyping from the IIDP Human Islet Phenotyping Program (HIPP), including measurements of purity, viability, insulin and glucagon response curves, hormone content, and cellular composition

Data and Resources

Explore IIDP datasets via the IIDP website or through PanKbase.

Funding

IIDP is sponsored by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), a component of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), and historical funding from The Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation (JDRF, now renamed as Breakthrough T1D).

More About the Resource

The Integrated Islet Distribution Project (IIDP) is the world’s largest initiative providing samples and data from human islets and related tissues for basic and translational research. IIDP provides access to high-quality human donor-derived pancreatic islets and related samples prepared following standardized processing, packaging, and shipping protocols in order to advance diabetes research.

Services provided by IIDP include:

  • Fair, equitable distribution of high-quality islets and non-islet biospecimens from the same donor
  • Islet-to-investigator matching
  • Investigator-specified islet and donor profiles required for studies
  • Provision of standardized islets to collaborating sites for the same study
  • Customizable data reports with donor data and islet isolation details
  • Genetic ancestry and partitioned genetic risk scores for type 1 and type 2 diabetes
  • Post-shipment islet phenotyping, including:
    • Measurements of purity, viability, potency, and hormone content
    • Histological analyses of cellular compositions, including percentage of endocrine versus exocrine cells and average percentages of α, β, and δ cells

More About the Team

Led by Co-Principal Investigators Dr. Joyce Niland and Dr. Carmella Evans-Molina, IIDP is housed at the City of Hope and subcontracts with ten US-based centers that provide high-quality isolated human islets and associated tissues. Subcontracted labs at Stanford University and Vanderbilt University provide genotyping and phenotyping data, respectively. For a summary of IIDP resources distributed to date, see here.
